paper_context.research_question: Can word-embedding-augmented IR term-weighting schemes applied to sentiment analysis of 10-K Risk Factors, alone or fused with market features, improve forecast accuracy of future stock volatility (quarterly/annual) compared to existing methods?
contribution_style: incremental methodological improvement (applying embedding-extended IR weighting to sentiment features)
comparative experimental study (benchmarks against prior work and market baselines)
analytic exploratory study (temporal drift and sectoral analyses)
main_claims: IR term-weighting schemes extended with word-embedding similarity (e.g., B̂M25, T̂C) produce stronger sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors and significantly improve volatility prediction performance over prior lexicon/expansion approaches.

Combining textual features derived from 10-K reports with market-derived features (current volatility, GARCH, sector) via stacking yields further performance gains and more stable long-horizon predictions than market features alone.
Recent reports (2012–2015) form more coherent clusters and produce better predictive models than older years due to conceptual drift; training on the most recent cluster improves results.

Although sectors exhibit distinct risk-term patterns, sector-specific models trained on the available data do not outperform a general model (likely due to limited per-sector training data); sector-aware analysis can nevertheless reveal useful term-sense disambiguations.
expected_evaluation_dimensions: Predictive accuracy on volatility targets (r^2 and MSE) comparing proposed text-only, market-only, and fused models against established baselines (GARCH, Wang et al., Tsai & Wang).
Ablation over term-weighting schemes (standard vs. embedding-extended: T̂C, B̂M25, etc.) and lexicon variants (Lex vs. LexExt).
Effectiveness of feature-fusion strategies (early fusion, stacking/late fusion, MKL) and their computational trade-offs.
Temporal generalization (training on past years and testing on subsequent years; sensitivity to concept drift / year clusters).

Sectoral robustness and data-size sensitivity (performance of general vs sector-specific vs sector-agnostic subsampled models; interpretability of feature coefficients for sector-specific term importance).
Statistical significance and practical relevance of improvements over baselines (consistency across cross-validation folds and quartile horizons).

extracted_claims.claim_text: Information Retrieval term-weighting schemes extended with word-embedding similarity (denoted T̂C, T̂F, T̂FIDF, B̂M25) produce stronger sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors than their standard counterparts and than prior lexicon-expansion approaches (e.g., Tsai & Wang), improving downstream volatility-prediction performance.
evidence: Definition of extension: t̂cdi(t) = tcdi(t) + sum_{t' in R(t)} sim(t,t') tcdi(t') with similarity threshold 0.70 (Section 4.1 eq.3).
Report that extended schemes (hat versions) improve upon normal forms; B̂M25, BM25, and T̂C show best results (Section 6.2, Table 1).
Comparison vs prior methods: Our method reported r2 0.439 (Text) and 0.527 (Text+Market) vs Wang (2013) and Tsai (2014) (Table 2).
uncertainty_flags: Exact statistical significance tests versus prior methods are not reported in the cited tables; magnitude and variance across folds is not fully detailed.
Improvement may depend on chosen hyperparameters (similarity threshold 0.70, Word2Vec trained on same corpus) and dimensionality reduction (PCA to 400 dims) — sensitivity analysis not shown.

extracted_claims.claim_label: text+market fusion via stacking yields further gains
extracted_claims.claim_text: Combining textual features derived from 10-K Risk Factors with market-derived features (current volatility, GARCH, sector) using stacking (late fusion) yields additional predictive performance and produces more stable long-horizon (later quartiles) volatility predictions than market-only or text-only models.
extracted_claims.section_anchor: Abstract; Methodology 4.3 (Feature Fusion); Market features 4.2; Experiments 6.2 (Figure 2a, Table 1, Table 2)
evidence: Description of stacking: split training 70%-30%, train base models on each modality, then train SVM-RBF meta-model (Section 4.3).
Table 2: Text+Market (Our method) r2 = 0.527 vs Text alone r2 = 0.439 and Market alone r2 = 0.485.
Figure 2a: plotted curves show Text+Market has higher r2 across quartiles and apparently decays slower than Market/GARCH dashed baselines.
uncertainty_flags: No statistical tests or confidence intervals shown for stacked vs other fusion methods (stacking vs MKL vs early fusion) besides point estimates.
Stacking protocol splits training set for meta-model — potential data-hunger effects acknowledged but not quantified (Section 4.3).

extracted_claims.claim_text: Reports from recent years (2012–2015) form a more coherent cluster (by centroid similarity) and models trained on this recent cluster provide better volatility prediction performance than models trained including older years (due to concept drift); therefore restricting training to 2012–2015 (3892 reports) improves results.
extracted_claims.section_anchor: Introduction; Experiments 6.1 (Figure 1a, Figure 1b, selection of 2012–2015 subset)
evidence: Figure 1a: cosine similarity heatmap of year-centroids showing three clusters: 2006–2008, 2009–2011, 2012–2015 (Section 6.1).
Figure 1b: r2 performance when progressively dropping oldest years improves; authors choose 2012–2015 subset of 3892 reports for remainder (Section 6.1).
uncertainty_flags: Cluster coherence is based on feature centroids from Tsai & Wang method — choice of representation may affect clustering result.
No formal concept-drift statistical test or out-of-sample holdout verification beyond the plotted cross-validation trend is reported.

extracted_claims.claim_text: The best-performing pipeline uses B̂M25 weighting with LexExt lexicon, PCA reduction to 400 dimensions, SVM-RBF base learners, and stacking for fusion; this configuration achieves the reported top results.
extracted_claims.section_anchor: Methodology 4.1 (weightings, PCA), 4.3 (stacking), Experiments 6.2 (Table 1, Table 2, paragraph selecting B̂M25 + LexExt + 400 dims + stacking)
evidence: Method details: B̂M25 defined as BM25 with tcdi replaced by t̂cdi (Section 4.1); LexExt described as lexicon expanded by top-20 Word2Vec neighbors (Section 4.1).
Authors state initial experiments show 400 PCA dims optimal, and they select B̂M25 + LexExt + stacking as best (Section 4.1 and 6.2).
Table 1 summarizes weighting scheme performance and fusion comparison; Table 2 compares final method vs baselines.
uncertainty_flags: 'Optimal' PCA dimension chosen from preliminary experiments but search details and validation procedure not fully reported.
Hyperparameter choices for SVM (C=1.0, epsilon=0.1) and Word2Vec training specifics are fixed but sensitivity not explored.

extracted_claims.claim_label: sectoral patterns exist but sector-specific models underperform
extracted_claims.claim_text: Different financial sectors exhibit distinct risk-term patterns and term-sense disambiguations (e.g., 'fire', 'beneficial'), but sector-specific models trained on available per-sector data do not outperform a general model — attributed to limited per-sector training sizes; however sector-aware analysis can reveal interpretable term importances.
extracted_claims.section_anchor: Market Features 4.2; Experiments 6.3 (Figures 2c, 3a, 3b; Table 3; sector term examples and analysis)
evidence: Figure 2c: per-sector r2 performance differences shown for Text and Text+Market.

Figure 3a/3b: comparisons of general model vs sector-specific vs sector-agnostic sampled-equal-size models show sector-specific underperforming general model; sector-agnostic (same-size) often similar to sector-specific, implicating sample size effect (Section 6.3).
Examples: 'fire' has high coefficient in energy sector due to domain sense; 'beneficial' appears negative in healthcare/basic industries due to 'beneficial owner' context (Section 6.3).
uncertainty_flags: Interpretation that underperformance is 'likely' due to sample size is plausible but not definitively proven (alternative causes like overfitting, domain feature mismatch not excluded).
Linear-regression coefficient interpretability relies on no PCA and sparse features — potential multicollinearity or stemming-induced ambiguity may affect coefficient reliability.

extracted_claims.claim_text: Text-derived features from 10-K Risk Factors provide more stable predictive signal over longer horizons (later quartiles) compared to market-only (GARCH/current volatility) models; fusing text with market features reduces performance decay at longer horizons.
extracted_claims.section_anchor: Experiments 6.2 (Figure 2a and related paragraph discussing decay across quartiles)
evidence: Figure 2a: plotted r2 curves across eight quartiles show GARCH and Market performance decays faster than Text, and Text+Market decays less than Market alone.
Authors' narrative: market-based methods decrease faster as historic prices become less relevant; textual features maintain similar performance across first four quartiles and decay slower.
uncertainty_flags: No formal temporal significance testing or confidence bands are provided for the quartile curves; visual differences could be sample-dependent.
Definition of quartiles uses fixed 64 trading-day windows; alternative horizon definitions might change observed stability.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: Word2Vec embeddings trained on the same corpus of 10-K Risk Factors yield reliable semantic similarities for term expansion (threshold 0.70 selects meaningful neighbors).
identified_assumptions.section_anchor: Methodology 4.1 (paragraph on LexExt and eq.3); references to Rekabsaz et al.
supporting_evidence: Authors state Word2Vec trained on corpus of all reports and use cosine similarity threshold 0.70 for R(t) selection (Section 4.1).
References to Rekabsaz et al. (2016a, 2017) for threshold choice.
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If embeddings are noisy or threshold miscalibrated, expansion may add irrelevant/antonymous terms, harming term weights and prediction; reported gains for extended schemes may not generalize.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: The Risk Factors section (Item 1A) extracted by term-matching heuristics reliably isolates the informative portion of 10-Ks relevant to volatility forecasting.
identified_assumptions.section_anchor: Dataset description Section 5 (extraction of Risk Factors using term matching heuristics)
supporting_evidence: Authors state they extract Risk Factors section using term matching heuristics and remove HTML tags, then stem (Section 5).
Justification referencing prior work noting Risk Factors usefulness (Dyer et al., Campbell et al.).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If extraction is imprecise (misses Risk Factors or includes unrelated text), features may be contaminated, reducing model validity and leading to over/underestimation of textual contribution.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: PCA to 400 dimensions preserves the predictive signal from high-dimensional lexicon-weight features while mitigating sparsity/overfitting.
supporting_evidence: Authors report initial experiments across 50–1000 dims showed 400 as optimum (Section 4.1).
Final pipeline uses PCA to 400 dims (Section 6.2).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If PCA discards informative directions or mixes features in a way that hurts interpretability/transferability, reported gains may be due to overfitting the cross-validation folds and may not generalize to future years.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: The SVM-RBF with chosen hyperparameters (C=1.0, epsilon=0.1) is an appropriate learner for the reduced feature space and comparison baselines (including GARCH and prior text methods) are trained/validated comparably.
supporting_evidence: Authors set C and epsilon equal to prior studies and report that RBF performed better than linear and cosine kernels in initial experiments (Section 4.1).
Baselines (GARCH, Market, Wang, Tsai) use SVM learner with RBF for GARCH/Market baselines per Section 5.
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If hyperparameters are suboptimal for baselines or for some feature sets, comparisons may favor the proposed pipeline; lack of hyperparameter tuning details per method could bias results.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: Filtering volatility outliers by removing values greater/smaller than mean ± 3 std preserves representative label distribution and does not bias predictive performance.
identified_assumptions.section_anchor: Dataset Section 5 (filtering volatility values > mean ± 3 std)
supporting_evidence: Authors state they filter volatility values outside mean ± 3*std (Section 5).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If extreme volatility events are informative and systematically correlated with textual cues, their removal could understate model usefulness for high-risk predictions and affect r2 comparisons.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: Year-cluster selection (using 2012–2015) improves model relevance to future reports because recent reports better represent future language and risk patterns.
supporting_evidence: Authors show improvement in r2 when dropping older years and claim conceptual drift; choose 2012–2015 subset (3892 reports) for remaining experiments.
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If future reports diverge from 2012–2015 patterns, models trained on that window may not generalize; selection could introduce temporal selection bias and overstate performance in cross-validation.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: One-hot encoding of sector as a market feature adequately captures sectoral effects in fusion and stacking experiments.
identified_assumptions.section_anchor: Market Features 4.2 (sector description and one-hot encoding)
supporting_evidence: Authors list sectors and state sector is converted to numerical representation using one-hot encoding (Section 4.2).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: One-hot encoding ignores similarity between sectors and can produce sparse features; this may limit the ability of market models to exploit sectoral structure, influencing fusion outcomes.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: Comparisons across methods using r2 (and MSE where comparable) from 5-fold cross-validation provide a fair assessment of relative performance.
supporting_evidence: Authors state r2 used as main metric and report 5-fold cross-validation averages (Section 5, Section 6.2).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If cross-validation folds are not stratified by company, sector, or time, leakage or temporal dependencies could inflate r2; lack of confidence intervals prevents assessing variability across folds.

identified_assumptions.assumption_text: The lexicon (Loughran & McDonald 2011) and its stemmed form (Porter) provide appropriate positive/negative/uncertain keyword sets for 10-K risk sentiment analysis.
supporting_evidence: Authors adopt Lex from Loughran & McDonald (2011) and follow prior works (Wang et al., Nopp & Hanbury) (Section 4.1).
identified_assumptions.risk_if_unmet: If lexicon entries are not well-suited to Risk Factors genre or stemming conflates distinct senses, term weights and expansions may misrepresent sentiment, affecting model validity (noted by examples like 'fire').

argument_focus: Efficacy of embedding-augmented IR term-weighting (esp. B̂M25) for constructing document-level sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors.
Effectiveness of feature-fusion strategies (stacking vs MKL vs early fusion) to combine textual and market features for volatility forecasting.
Temporal dataset selection and concept drift: rationale and impact of using 2012–2015 subset.
Sectoral analysis: presence of domain-specific term senses and trade-off between sector-specific models vs general model given sample sizes.
contribution_targets: Methodological adaptation: transferring embedding-augmented IR weighting schemes to sentiment feature construction for long documents (10-K Risk Factors).
Empirical benchmarking: comparing proposed text-only and text+market pipelines against prior lexical and expansion baselines (Wang et al., Tsai & Wang) and market baselines (GARCH, Market).
Data characterization: documenting temporal clusters (2006–2008, 2009–2011, 2012–2015) and sectoral term-sense observations.
evaluation_targets: Validate that embedding-extended weighting schemes (T̂*, B̂M25) statistically outperform their standard counterparts and prior lexicon-expansion baselines across folds and temporal splits.
Assess sensitivity of results to Word2Vec training choices (corpus, hyperparameters), similarity threshold (0.70), and number of expansion neighbors (top-20).
Check robustness to PCA dimensionality (range 50–1000) and hyperparameter tuning of SVM (C, epsilon, kernel) and stacking split ratios.
Verify extraction quality of Risk Factors (term-matching heuristics) and impact of possible label filtering (mean ±3 std removal) on performance.
Test generalization to temporally realistic splits (train on past, test on a held-out future year) with no data leakage and report uncertainty (CI, fold variance).
Quantify whether sector-specific underperformance is due to training-set size vs inherent domain transfer limits, e.g., via learning curves and cross-sector transfer experiments.
uncertainty_flags: Lack of reported statistical significance tests, confidence intervals, or fold-level variances for key comparisons (Tables 1,2; Figures).
Hyperparameter sensitivity and ablation details (Word2Vec training specs, PCA tuning, SVM kernel/hyperparameters per baseline) are underreported.
Risk of temporal leakage: cross-validation protocol may not fully account for temporal dependence unless folds are time-aware; only a few temporal-split experiments are shown.
Risk-factor extraction heuristics and volatility outlier filtering may materially affect results but are not fully detailed.
chaining_notes: Downstream reviewers should: (1) test robustness of claims C1–C4 by reproducing embedding-training and expansion steps (Word2Vec parameters, threshold 0.70, top-20 neighbors), (2) evaluate statistical significance and fold-level variability for reported r2/MSE differences, and (3) validate temporal generalization via strictly time-ordered train/test splits (no future info in training).
Investigate A2 (Risk Factors extraction) by sampling extracted sections vs ground-truth/manual annotations to quantify extraction accuracy and its effect on features.
For sectoral claims, run learning-curve experiments to separate sample-size effects from domain specificity and test alternative sector encodings (hierarchical/embeddings) beyond one-hot.
Conduct sensitivity analyses for PCA dimension and SVM hyperparameters; report confidence intervals and include ablations removing embedding expansion to isolate its marginal contribution.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The manuscript argues that embedding-augmented IR term-weighting (T̂C, T̂F, T̂FIDF, B̂M25) produces stronger sentiment features from 10-K Risk Factors, improving volatility prediction versus prior lexicon methods. It further claims that stacking-based fusion of text and market features yields additional gains and longer-horizon stability, that selecting a recent year-cluster (2012–2015) mitigates concept drift for improved performance, and that sectoral term-sense differences exist though sector-specific models underperform the general model likely due to limited per-sector data. The argument chain is coherent and implemented end-to-end (extraction -> embedding-augmentation eq.3 -> IR weightings -> PCA -> SVM-RBF -> fusion), but key methodological gaps weaken claim strength: missing statistical uncertainty, limited sensitivity analyses for embeddings/PCA/SVM, potential temporal leakage in CV, and under-validated Risk Factors extraction and outlier filtering. Addressing these would substantially strengthen claim-to-evidence linkage and external validity.
logical_argument_graph: Problem framing: volatility forecasting can benefit from textual signals in 10-K Risk Factors.
Data extraction: Risk Factors (Item 1A) are extracted via heuristics; volatility labels computed as realized volatility over 64-day quartiles.
Lexicon features: construct Lex and LexExt (Loughran & McDonald; top-20 Word2Vec neighbors).
Embedding augmentation: extend term counts using t̂cdi(t) = tcdi(t) + sum_{t' in R(t)} sim(t,t') tcdi(t') (Eq.3, threshold 0.70).
IR weighting: apply TC/TF/TFIDF/BM25 and their hat-variants using t̂cdi where applicable.
Dimension reduction & learning: PCA to 400 dims followed by SVM-RBF regression (C=1.0, ε=0.1).
Fusion strategies: early fusion (concatenate), stacking (70/30 base/meta), MKL (mklaren approximation).
Evaluation: primary 5-fold CV on 2012–2015 subset (3892 reports), temporal holdouts for 2013/2014/2015, sector splits and sector-agnostic controls.

Claims supported by Tables/Figures: (C1) hat-weightings improve r2; (C2) stacking Text+Market improves further; (C3) recent-year subset helps; (C4) B̂M25+LexExt+PCA400+stacking best; (C5) sectoral term patterns exist but sector-specific models underperform; (C6) text yields longer-horizon stability.

Critical weak links: missing uncertainty quantification (no CIs or per-fold variances), insufficient hyperparameter/sensitivity ablations (Word2Vec, threshold, top-k, PCA dims, SVM tuning), potential temporal leakage in CV, and under-validated Risk Factors extraction and label filtering.

evidence: Figure 2a: plotted r2 across eight quartiles shows GARCH and Market decay faster than Text; Text+Market decays less than Market alone.
Authors' rationale that market historic prices lose relevance over time while textual cues remain informative.
uncertainty_flags: No confidence bands or formal temporal significance testing for quartile curves; visual differences may be sample-dependent.
Quarter definition (64 trading days) is a design choice; alternate horizons might change observed stability.

strengths.title: Clear methodological adaptation of embedding-augmented IR weighting
strengths.description: The paper formalizes embedding-augmented weighting (Eq.3) and applies it systematically across multiple IR schemes, enabling an interpretable pipeline for enriching lexicon-based term counts in long documents.
evidence: Equation 3 and definitions of T̂C, T̂F, T̂FIDF, B̂M25.
Citations to Rekabsaz et al. for threshold rationale and IR parameter choices.

strengths.title: Comprehensive empirical comparisons with relevant baselines
strengths.description: Experiments compare proposed methods against established baselines (GARCH, Market, Wang et al., Tsai & Wang) and evaluate multiple fusion strategies (stacking, MKL, early fusion) across text-only and fused settings.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 provide r2 and MSE comparisons; Figures show temporal and sectoral analyses.

strengths.title: Attention to temporal and sectoral heterogeneity
strengths.description: The manuscript inspects year-clustering (concept drift), performs temporal holdouts, and runs sector-split analyses with sector-agnostic controls to probe where methods help and where data limits performance.
evidence: Figure 1a/1b for year clusters and performance trends; Section 6.3 sector experiments with controls.

concerns.title: Lack of statistical uncertainty quantification
concerns.description: Key performance claims rely on point estimates (r2 and MSE) without reporting confidence intervals, fold-level variances, or statistical tests comparing methods; this weakens the strength of claimed improvements.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 present mean r2 and MSE but no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or p-values.
Figures (quartile curves, sector bars) lack error bands or per-fold dispersion.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report per-fold metrics (r2/MSE), compute 95% CIs or conduct paired tests (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank or paired t-tests) for top method vs baselines; add error bands to plots.

concerns.title: Insufficient sensitivity analyses for embedding and hyperparameters
concerns.description: Embedding-expansion (Word2Vec training specs, vector size, context window, top-k neighbors, similarity threshold 0.70), PCA dim (400), and SVM hyperparameters are fixed and under-documented; robustness to these choices is unclear.
evidence: Threshold 0.70 and top-20 neighbors cited from Rekabsaz et al. but no ablation on threshold or neighbor count.
PCA dim reported as chosen from initial tests but selection procedure and validation not detailed; SVM tuning not described per baseline.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide ablations varying similarity threshold (e.g., 0.6–0.9), neighbor counts (5/10/20/50), Word2Vec hyperparameters, PCA dims (e.g., 100, 200, 400, 800), and run hyperparameter searches for SVM across methods, reporting effect on r2 and stability.

concerns.title: Potential temporal leakage in cross-validation and dataset selection
concerns.description: 5-fold CV on pooled reports (even within 2012–2015) may mix temporally correlated documents and risk leakage; temporal holdouts are limited and do not fully confirm out-of-time generalization.
evidence: Primary evaluation uses 5-fold CV; temporal holdouts reported only for 2013/2014/2015 with modest differences.
Selection of 2012–2015 subset based on centroid coherence could be circular if CV folds are time-mixed.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Adopt strictly time-ordered train/test splits across multiple future-year holdouts (train on years ≤ t, test on year t+1), ensure CV folds do not mix future reports into training, and report results to demonstrate temporal generalization.

concerns.title: Risk Factors extraction and label filtering under-validated
concerns.description: Extraction of Risk Factors via heuristics and filtering of volatility outliers (> mean ± 3σ) are operational choices that could materially affect features/labels but lack validation.
evidence: Section 5 describes heuristic extraction and ±3σ filtering; no manual spot-checks or sensitivity tests reported.
Shared analysis flags A2 and A5 that quantify risk if these assumptions fail.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide a manual annotation sample (e.g., 50–100 reports) to measure extraction precision/recall, test model performance with/without outlier filtering, and analyze whether extreme volatilities align with textual signals.

concerns.title: Comparability of baselines and hyperparameter tuning
concerns.description: Reproduced baselines (Wang, Tsai, GARCH, Market) lack clear, equal hyperparameter tuning protocols, risking biased comparisons.
evidence: SVM C and ε follow prior studies but per-baseline tuning procedure not reported; GARCH details deferred to supplementary materials.
Fairness in preprocessing (PCA application, feature scaling) across baselines not fully specified.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run standardized hyperparameter searches per baseline (and report ranges/grids), ensure identical preprocessing steps where applicable, and include GARCH implementation details for reproducibility.

concerns.title: Interpretability claims need diagnostic checks
concerns.description: Interpretation of term importance via linear regression coefficients (sectoral examples) is informative but requires diagnostics for collinearity, stemming ambiguity, and coefficient stability.
evidence: Term examples (fire, beneficial) presented without bootstrap CIs, VIFs, or contextual concordance analyses.
Authors trained linear regression without PCA for interpretability but omitted diagnostics.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide coefficient stability measures (bootstrap CIs), multicollinearity diagnostics (VIF), and extract representative sentence contexts for highlighted terms to validate interpretive claims.

Authors state dataset available via anonymous URL; code and exact scripts for training Word2Vec, building t̂cdi, PCA, and stacking protocol should be shared to enable reproduction.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes using word-embedding-augmented IR term-weighting (extended tcdi via cosine-similarity neighbors) to build sentiment features from 10-K Risk Factors and uses PCA + SVM-RBF to predict future stock volatility. It compares standard and embedding-extended weightings (TC/TF/TFIDF/BM25 and hat-variants), tests lexicon expansion (Lex vs LexExt), and fuses textual features with market features via early fusion, MKL, and stacking. Experiments use SEC 10-K Risk Factors (2006–2015), but focus on a 2012–2015 subset (3892 reports) justified by centroid cosine-similarity clustering. Main empirical claims are that embedding-extended IR weightings (notably B̂M25) improve text-features and forecasting, stacking Text+Market further improves results and stabilizes long-term horizons, recent-year training mitigates concept drift, and sector-specific models underperform general models due primarily to limited per-sector data. Methodological gaps include underreported statistical significance, potential temporal leakage in cross-validation, limited sensitivity analyses (Word2Vec, similarity threshold, PCA dims, SVM tuning), incomplete description/validation of Risk Factors extraction heuristics, and handling of volatility outliers. The reported numerical improvements (e.g., Text r2 from 0.395→0.439; Text+Market r2 0.484/0.499→0.527) are promising but need robustness checks (CI, fold variances, temporally ordered splits, hyperparameter sensitivity) to support causal attribution to embedding-augmentation and fusion choices.
logical_argument_graph: Long 10-K Risk Factors contain risk signals relevant to future volatility (premise supported by prior literature and intuition).
Lexicon-based sentiment features built over Risk Factors can be improved by IR term-weighting schemes to better reflect term importance in long documents (apply BM25, TC, etc.).
Word embeddings capture lexical similarity; extending term counts to include similar words (thresholded cosine neighbors) creates denser, semantically-aware term weights (eq.3).
Embedding-extended weighting (t̂cdi) improves document sentiment feature quality versus standard tcdi, yielding better predictive power for volatility (observed r2 gains).
Dimensionality reduction (PCA to 400) mitigates high-dimensional sparsity and aids SVM-RBF learning on these features.
Fusing text with market features (stacking) combines complementary signals and further increases r2 and long-horizon stability.
Temporal drift observed in centroid similarity motivates restricting training to recent years (2012–2015) to improve model relevance.
Sector-specific term senses exist; however, small per-sector train sizes explain why sector-specific models underperform a general model.

identified_claims.claim_text: Information Retrieval term-weighting schemes extended with word-embedding similarity (denoted T̂C, T̂F, T̂FIDF, B̂M25) produce stronger sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors than their standard counterparts and than prior lexicon-expansion approaches (e.g., Tsai & Wang), improving downstream volatility-prediction performance.
evidence: Definition of t̂cdi(t) (Eq.3) and use of sim threshold 0.70 (Methodology 4.1).
Table 1: hat-variants (B̂M25, T̂C) show higher Text r2 than non-hat variants; Table 2: Our method Text r2 = 0.439 vs Tsai 0.395 and Wang 0.345.

Sensitivity of results to Word2Vec training choices (corpus, params), similarity threshold (0.70), and neighbor count (top-20 used for LexExt) not explored.

evidence: Stacking protocol described (70-30 split; SVM-RBF meta-model) in 4.3.
Table 2: Text+Market Our method r2 = 0.527 > Market 0.485 and Text 0.439; Figure 2a shows slower decay across quartiles for Text+Market.
uncertainty_flags: No confidence intervals or statistical comparisons of stacking vs MKL vs early fusion; stacking uses reduced training for base/meta models which could bias results.
Potential overfitting or data-hunger effects of stacking not quantified.

identified_claims.claim_text: Reports from recent years (2012–2015) form more coherent clusters and models trained on this recent cluster provide better volatility prediction performance than models trained including older years, due to conceptual drift.

Figure 1b: r2 improves as oldest years are dropped; authors select 2012–2015 subset (3892 reports).
uncertainty_flags: Clustering based on Tsai & Wang feature representation; no formal statistical test for concept drift or out-of-sample validation on a future held-out year beyond limited experiments.
Potential selection bias: choosing the recent window because it maximizes cross-validated r2 may overfit to idiosyncratic recent patterns.

identified_claims.claim_text: The best-performing pipeline uses B̂M25 weighting with LexExt lexicon, PCA reduction to 400 dimensions, SVM-RBF base learners, and stacking for fusion; this configuration achieves the reported top results.

Table 1 & 2: authors report B̂M25 + LexExt + 400 dims + stacking as best-performing.

No ablation isolating PCA dimension effect or per-component contribution (e.g., B̂M25 without PCA) shown.

Linear-regression coefficient interpretability could be confounded by multicollinearity, stemming artifacts, or undocumented preprocessing choices.

identified_claims.claim_text: Text-derived features provide more stable predictive signal over longer horizons compared to market-only models; fusing text with market features reduces performance decay at longer horizons.
evidence: Figure 2a: r2 across 8 quartiles shows Text decays less than Market/GARCH; Text+Market decays slower than Market alone.
Authors' rationale: market signals become less relevant over longer horizons; textual content remains informative.
uncertainty_flags: No confidence bands or statistical tests for quartile curves; horizon definition fixed to 64-trading-day quartiles—alternate horizons not evaluated.
Possibility that cross-validation approach mixes temporal info, inflating apparent stability.

strengths.title: Clear methodological adaptation of embedding-augmented IR to sentiment
strengths.description: The paper adapts recent IR weighting methods that incorporate word-embedding similarities (eq.3) to construct sentiment features for long documents (10-K Risk Factors), which is a methodologically coherent transfer.
evidence: Equation 3 defining t̂cdi using embedding-based similarity and references to Rekabsaz et al. (2016a, 2016b, 2017).
Comparisons of hat vs non-hat variants in Table 1 showing consistent improvements.

strengths.title: Comprehensive experimental comparison across fusions and baselines
strengths.description: Authors compare multiple weighting schemes, lexicon variants, fusion strategies (early, stacking, MKL), and market baselines (GARCH, Market), enabling multi-angle evaluation.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 include different weightings and fusion methods; Figure 2a shows temporal decay comparisons.
Baselines reimplemented: Wang (2013), Tsai (2014), GARCH, Market.

strengths.title: Attention to temporal and sectoral data characteristics
strengths.description: Study includes analysis of temporal clusters (centroid cosine similarity) and sector-level term-sense examples, addressing nonstationarity and domain heterogeneity.
evidence: Figure 1a heatmap and Figure 1b trending performance when older years dropped.
Sector examples (fire, beneficial) and sector performance plots (Figures 2c, 3a, 3b).

concerns.title: Lack of statistical significance and uncertainty reporting
concerns.description: Key reported improvements (r2 differences across methods and fusion strategies) are presented as point estimates without confidence intervals, per-fold variances, or hypothesis tests, limiting confidence that gains are robust and not sampling noise.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 show r2 and MSE averages but no standard deviations, CIs, or p-values.
Figures (e.g., 2a quartile curves) lack error bands across folds.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report fold-level statistics (mean ± std), bootstrap confidence intervals for r2/MSE differences, and statistical tests (paired t-test or Wilcoxon) comparing top methods (e.g., B̂M25 vs BM25, stacking vs early fusion).

concerns.title: Potential temporal leakage in cross-validation
concerns.description: 5-fold cross-validation may not be time-aware; if training and test folds mix reports from different years in a way that allows future information to influence training (e.g., via PCA or Word2Vec trained on full corpus), reported performance could be optimistic.
evidence: Paper trains Word2Vec 'on the corpus of all the reports' and applies PCA and cross-validation on same dataset; temporal-split experiments are limited to a few year-held-out tests without full leakage-control description.
Authors note temporal experiments for 2013,2014,2015 but bulk results use CV on 2012–2015 subset.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Clarify whether embedding/PCA were trained strictly within training folds; rerun experiments with strictly time-ordered training/test splits (rolling-origin) and train Word2Vec/PCA on training portion only to avoid future leakage.

concerns.title: Insufficient sensitivity analyses for embedding and expansion hyperparameters
concerns.description: Central transformation (t̂cdi) depends on Word2Vec training, cosine similarity threshold (0.70), and selection of neighbors (top-20 for LexExt). The robustness of results to these choices is not demonstrated.
evidence: Methodology fixes threshold=0.70 per Rekabsaz but no ablation shown; LexExt uses top-20 neighbors per Tsai & Wang but no sensitivity reported; Word2Vec training details (window, dim, epochs) not provided.
Uncertainty flags in shared analysis note missing sensitivity analysis.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide Word2Vec training hyperparameters; report results for thresholds (e.g., 0.60, 0.70, 0.80), neighbor counts (5, 10, 20, 50), and at least one alternative embedding (GloVe or pretrained financial embeddings) to test generality.

concerns.title: PCA and SVM hyperparameter selection under-documented
concerns.description: PCA dimension (400) and SVM RBF hyperparameters (C=1.0, epsilon=0.1) are set with cursory explanation; absence of protocol details (validation folds, seeds) risks overfitting and obscures reproducibility.
evidence: Text states 'initial experiments show 400 dimension as optimum' but no search grid, curves, or reproducible selection method is provided.
SVM hyperparameters set 'similar to previous studies' and RBF chosen via 'initial experiments', but no systematic tuning reported across methods/baselines.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Document hyperparameter search ranges, selection procedure (nested CV or separate validation), random seeds; include an ablation table showing performance vs PCA dims and SVM C/gamma to demonstrate stability.

concerns.title: Risk Factors extraction validation missing
concerns.description: Extraction of Item 1A Risk Factors uses term-matching heuristics but no quantitative evaluation (precision/recall) or error analysis is provided to assess whether extracted sections are accurate and comparable across years.
evidence: Section 5 states Risk Factors extracted via term matching heuristics; no corpus of manual labels or extraction accuracy statistics provided.
Shared analysis flags that mis-extraction could contaminate features and bias results.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide extraction algorithm details and validate on a sample of filings with manual annotations (report extraction precision/recall). If imperfect, include sensitivity test (use only manually-verified extracts for subset) to measure impact.

concerns.title: Outlier filtering of volatility may bias results
concerns.description: Filtering volatility labels outside mean ± 3 std removes extreme events that might be most relevant to textual risk signals; this could bias evaluation toward average behaviors.
evidence: Dataset description in Section 5 notes filtering volatility values > mean ± 3*std with no exploration of impact.
If extreme volatility events coincide with strong textual signals, removal weakens the estimated predictive power of text.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report experiments with and without outlier filtering; quantify how many samples were removed and whether removed cases are concentrated in certain years/sectors; consider robust metrics or heavy-tail-aware models instead of hard filtering.

concerns.title: Sectoral attribution not disentangled from sample-size effects
concerns.description: Conclusion that sector-specific models underperform due to small per-sector training sizes is plausible but insufficiently supported; alternative explanations (overfitting, feature mismatch, sector encoding) are not excluded.
evidence: Figures 3a/3b show sector-specific lower bars and sector-agnostic same-size sampled models similar to sector-specific, suggesting sample-size effect, but no learning curves or cross-sector transfer tests are shown.
One-hot sector encoding is used which ignores sector similarity structure.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run learning curves (performance vs training size per sector), cross-sector transfer tests (train on other sectors then fine-tune), and alternative sector encodings (hierarchical grouping or sector embeddings) to isolate sample-size vs domain mismatch effects.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The manuscript adapts embedding-augmented IR term-weighting schemes (per Rekabsaz et al.) to produce document-level sentiment features from long 10-K Risk Factors, applies PCA reduction and SVM regression, and evaluates these features alone and fused with market features (stacking, MKL, early fusion) for forecasting future stock volatility. Empirically, the extended weightings (e.g., B̂M25, T̂C) using Word2Vec-based similarity (threshold 0.70) outperform standard weighting and prior lexicon-expansion baselines (Tsai & Wang, Wang et al.) under 5-fold CV on a 2012–2015 subset. Stacking of text and market modalities yields further gains and appears to stabilize longer-horizon forecasts. The paper also documents temporal clustering (centroid cosine similarity) motivating use of recent-year training window, and reports that sector-specific models underperform a general model—likely due to limited per-sector sample sizes—while revealing interpretable sector-specific term-sense differences. Overall, the work is an incremental methodological application and comprehensive empirical benchmarking that combines established IR-embedding ideas with volatility forecasting tasks, but several methodological and reporting gaps limit the strength of novelty and generalization claims.
logical_argument_graph: Problem: Volatility can be forecasted from text (10-K Risk Factors) and market features — prior work used lexicons and word-embedding term expansion (Wang, Tsai).

Idea: Use embedding-augmented IR term weighting (t̂cdi via sim-weighted expansion of tcdi) to produce denser and semantically-aware lexicon-weight features for long documents (Rekabsaz et al. adaptation).
Pipeline: extract Risk Factors → apply Lex / LexExt → compute standard and extended weighting schemes (TC, TF, TFIDF, BM25; T̂* / B̂M25) → PCA(400) → SVM-RBF regression.
Fusion: combine text and market features using early fusion, MKL, and stacking (stacking: 70/30 split of training to build meta-model).

Empirical claim: On 2012–2015 subset (3892 reports), extended weightings (B̂M25, T̂C) outperform baselines (Tsai & Wang, Wang) with Text r2 up to 0.439 and Text+Market r2 up to 0.527 (Table 1, Table 2).
Temporal analysis: year-centroid similarities show three clusters; dropping older years improves CV performance, motivating 2012–2015 subset selection (Fig 1).
Sector findings: sectors show distinct term importance; sector-specific models underperform general model, likely due to limited per-sector data (Figs 2c, 3a/3b).

Conclusion: Embedding-augmented IR weighting produces incremental but meaningful improvement for volatility prediction when combined with market features; however, robustness, hyperparameter sensitivity, and statistical uncertainty need fuller evaluation.

Demonstrated performance gains in Table 1 where extended schemes outperform non-extended.

strengths.title: Comprehensive empirical benchmarking
strengths.description: Evaluates multiple weighting schemes, lexicon variants, fusion strategies, and compares against established baselines (GARCH, Wang, Tsai) on an openly-specified dataset and metrics.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 compare weighting schemes and Text/Market/Text+Market baselines.
Fusion experiments include stacking, MKL, and early fusion (Section 4.3; Table 1).

strengths.title: Temporal and sectoral analyses add interpretive depth
strengths.description: The year-centroid clustering and per-sector term examples provide useful data-characterization beyond raw predictive numbers.
evidence: Fig 1a/1b show year-cluster behavior and motivate 2012–2015 subset choice.
Sector examples (fire, beneficial owner) illuminate stemming/ambiguity issues (Section 6.3).

strengths.title: Practical fusion strategy exploration
strengths.description: Compares computational and predictive trade-offs of stacking vs MKL and early fusion with clear operational descriptions.
evidence: Stacking described with 70/30 split and RBF meta-model (Section 4.3); MKL implementation via mklaren referenced.
Empirical ordering stacking > MKL > early fusion in reported point estimates (Table 1).

concerns.title: Lack of statistical significance and fold variability
concerns.description: Key performance differences between extended and baseline methods are reported as point estimates (r2/MSE) but no confidence intervals, standard deviations across folds, or formal statistical tests are provided to assess whether reported gains are robust.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 show only mean r2 and MSE values; absence of error bars or p-values is noted in shared analysis.
Uncertainty flags in shared analysis explicitly call out missing fold-level variances.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report per-fold r2 (or bootstrapped CIs) and conduct paired statistical tests (e.g., paired t-test or Wilcoxon) comparing proposed method to closest baselines; include effect sizes.

concerns.title: Hyperparameter and embedding-sensitivity underreporting
concerns.description: Critical choices—Word2Vec training details, expansion neighbor count, similarity threshold (0.70), PCA dimension (400), SVM hyperparameters, stacking split—are fixed or briefly justified but lack systematic sensitivity analyses to show robustness.
evidence: Method states threshold 0.70 and top-20 neighbors (LexExt) but sensitivity to threshold/neighbors is not shown (Section 4.1).
Authors state 400 PCA dims chosen from 50–1000 exploratory search but do not report nested validation or holdout used for selection.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide ablation/sensitivity studies: vary similarity threshold (e.g., 0.6–0.8), top-N neighbors (5,10,20,50), Word2Vec hyperparameters, PCA dims and SVM tuning; report impact on r2 and stability.

concerns.title: Potential temporal leakage and non-time-aware CV
concerns.description: The main evaluation uses 5-fold cross-validation but does not clearly state whether folds are constructed to avoid temporal leakage (e.g., company-level or time-ordered splits). This can inflate predictive performance for time-dependent forecasting tasks.
evidence: Experiment Setup (Section 5) reports 5-fold CV but year-split experiments are presented separately; shared analysis flags risk of temporal leakage.
Realistic year-ordered tests are reported only for three single-year holdouts (Fig 2b) and show somewhat lower performance, suggesting CV may be optimistic.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Adopt strictly time-ordered train/test splits (rolling-origin) as primary evaluation for forecasting; ensure no future information from same company leaks into training folds and report results alongside CV.

concerns.title: Risk-factor extraction & label filtering under-specified
concerns.description: Extraction of Item 1A Risk Factors is done via term-matching heuristics and volatility labels are filtered by mean±3σ; neither extraction accuracy nor the impact of label filtering on results is quantified.
evidence: Section 5 states Risk Factors extracted via heuristics and HTML removal but no precision/recall against manual extraction is provided.
Volatility outliers removed by ±3 std (Section 5); shared analysis notes potential bias if extreme events are informative.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide extraction validation on a sample (manual check), report sensitivity of results to outlier removal (with/without filtering), and describe heuristics precisely (rules/patterns used).

concerns.title: Causal and counterfactual claims not supported
concerns.description: The narrative sometimes implies that removing older years reduces 'noise' from concept drift and that text features 'cause' longer-horizon stability; while plausible, causal claims are not rigorously tested.
evidence: Fig 1b and associated discussion claim dropping old years improves performance due to conceptual drift (Section 6.1).
Text argues market features decay in predictive power over time and textual features remain stable (Section 6.2) without formal causal tests.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Tone down causal language; run targeted experiments (e.g., concept-drift detection, transfer experiments training on old years and testing on later ones) to support causal interpretations.

comparable_works.similarity_or_difference: Similarity: use of Loughran-McDonald lexicon and SVM regression; Difference: current work modifies weighting via embedding-IR extension and fusion with market features.

uncertainty_flags: Main reported results are CV point estimates without fold-level dispersion or formal tests — risk that gains are not statistically robust.
Key hyperparameters (Word2Vec, sim threshold 0.70, top-20 neighbors, PCA dims, SVM kernel params) lack sensitivity analysis — results may be contingent.
Potential temporal leakage in CV and limited time-ordered holdout experiments mean reported r2 may be optimistic for real forecasting.
Risk-factor extraction heuristics and volatility outlier filtering effects not quantified — possible dataset-induced biases.
alternative_interpretations: Observed gains from extended weighting might derive primarily from smoothing/density increase of features (via expansion) rather than better semantic matching; simple densification or alternative dimensionality methods might recover similar gains.
Performance improvements in CV could be inflated by company-level or temporal overlap across folds; year-ordered tests show modest drops suggesting some optimism in CV numbers.

Stacking wins in point estimates possibly because base learners' hyperparameters (and kernel choices) were not equally tuned across fusion methods; MKL's underperformance might be an implementation/tuning artifact.
transparency_notes: Authors cite Rekabsaz et al. for threshold=0.70 but should report Word2Vec training details (vector size, window, min-count, epochs) and exact LexExt construction steps to enable reproducibility.
PCA dimension selection needs to be reported with search procedure and whether selection was nested inside CV to avoid leakage.
Provide code/data release (anonymized links referenced) and precise extraction heuristics for Risk Factors to enable replication and validation of extraction quality.

creativity_safeguard.novelty_not_validity_note: The paper adapts and assembles existing components (embedding-augmented IR weighting, lexicon-based sentiment, PCA, SVM, stacking) and applies them in a new combination to 10-K volatility forecasting. This constitutes an incremental methodological advance rather than a disruptive novelty; novelty does not substitute for rigorous methodological validation.
counterfactual_conditions_for_success: If Word2Vec trained on a substantially larger or more diverse financial corpus yields consistent similar-neighbor lists and retention of lexical polarity, embedding-augmented weighting will generalize well.
If PCA dimensionality and SVM hyperparameters are selected via strict nested validation and results remain stable, the claimed gains will be robust.
If time-ordered holdout evaluations reproduce or only modestly reduce CV gains, the methods will be applicable in real forecasting settings.
If risk-factor extraction heuristics are validated to have high precision/recall, the text signal is likely reliable; failure here would undermine the approach.

novelty_lenses.rationale: Adopts embedding-augmented IR weighting from IR literature and applies it to lexicon-based sentiment for long financial documents; the adaptation is principled and yields empirical gains versus immediate baselines.
evidence: t̂cdi formulation (eq.3) referencing Rekabsaz et al.; improved r2 for B̂M25 over BM25 in Table 1.
uncertainty_flags: Lack of sensitivity analyses and statistical tests reduces confidence that adaptation universally improves performance.

novelty_lenses.rationale: Comprehensive comparisons (weightings, lexicon variants, fusion strategies) and temporal/sectoral analyses provide valuable empirical evidence for the community about what combinations perform well on 10-K volatility tasks.
evidence: Tables 1/2, Figures 1/2/3, sector sample-size experiments with sector-agnostic sampling.
uncertainty_flags: Evaluations rely heavily on CV point estimates and a single PCA/hyperparameter setting—limits generalizability.

novelty_lenses.rationale: No new algorithmic theory is proposed; core novelty is application/combination rather than new modeling principles. The idea (using embedding similarity to augment term weights) is previously established in IR and reused here.
evidence: Rekabsaz et al. citations and reuse of their t̂cdi concept; no new mathematical derivation beyond substitution into standard weightings.
uncertainty_flags: Potential for a modest mechanistic insight if the paper demonstrates why IR-style augmentation better captures sentiment in long-form legal/financial prose, but this is not deeply analyzed.

confidence_interval.rationale: Assessment confidence is moderate: I am confident about the paper being an incremental and useful empirical contribution (supported by reported gains and clear adaptation of prior IR work), but reduced by methodological gaps (statistics, hyperparameter sensitivity, potential temporal leakage) that materially affect the strength of claims; thus a moderate confidence interval in the assessment.

specialist_reviews.analytical_summary: The paper proposes transferring embedding-augmented IR term-weighting techniques (originally applied in document retrieval) to construct sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors for stock volatility forecasting. The core technical move is to expand each lexicon term's document count tcdi(t) into t̂cdi(t) by adding cosine-weighted counts of semantically similar tokens (Word2Vec neighbors with similarity threshold 0.70), then plug t̂cdi into standard weighting formulas (TC/TF/TFIDF/BM25) producing T̂* and B̂M25 variants. These dense(er) lexicon-weight vectors are PCA-reduced (selected at 400 dims) and used with SVM-RBF regressors; textual and market modalities are combined primarily via stacking (late fusion), with MKL and early fusion also evaluated. Empirically, the authors select the recent 2012–2015 subset after observing year-centroid cosine clusters and show (5-fold CV) that B̂M25+LexExt+PCA(400)+SVM-RBF+Stacking outperforms prior lexicon and expansion baselines (Wang 2013; Tsai & Wang 2014) and market-only/GARCH baselines on first-year and longer-horizon volatility (r2 and MSE reported). Sectoral analysis finds distinct term-sense patterns but shows sector-specific models underperform a general model; the authors attribute this to limited per-sector sample sizes. The paper's argument chain: (1) word embeddings capture useful term similarity missing in raw lexicon counts; (2) propagating similarity-weighted counts into IR weights better captures document risk signal in long, redundant 10-Ks; (3) PCA and SVM-RBF make the enriched features tractable and predictive; (4) stacking fuses complementary text and market signals and stabilizes long-horizon performance; (5) temporal selection (2012–2015) mitigates concept drift and improves predictive relevance. The manuscript delivers coherent evidence (tables/figures) for these steps but leaves several robustness, statistical-significance, and reproducibility gaps unclosed (hyperparameter sensitivity, fold variance/CIs, extraction quality, potential temporal leakage).
logical_argument_graph: Node A: 10-K Risk Factors are useful but long/redundant (Dyer2016) -> motivates improved feature construction for long documents.
Node B: Existing lexicon+count methods underperform on long 10-Ks (Wang2013, Tsai2014) -> need for richer term representation.
Node C: Word2Vec trained on corpus yields semantically-similar terms R(t) (A1) -> allows expansion of counts via eq.3 to create t̂cdi(t).
Node D: Replace tcdi with t̂cdi in IR weight formulas -> T̂*, B̂M25 produce denser/more informative document weights.
Node E: PCA(400) reduces sparsity and overfitting risk -> yields tractable input for SVM-RBF.
Node F: SVM-RBF regression on text-only features improves volatility r2 vs prior baselines (Table 2).
Node G: Late fusion (stacking) combining text+market further improves r2 and stabilizes longer horizons (Figure 2a, Table 1).
Node H: Year-centroid cosine clusters indicate concept drift -> selecting 2012–2015 improves model relevance/performance.
Node I: Sectoral patterns show term-sense differences but sector-specific models underperform general model, likely due to limited samples.
Edges: A->B motivates C; C->D implements main novelty; D+E->F empirical claim C1; F+G->improved fused claims C2 and C6; H supports training window claim C3; I arises from sector experiments C5.

identified_claims.claim_text: Information Retrieval term-weighting schemes extended with word-embedding similarity (T̂C, T̂F, T̂FIDF, B̂M25) produce stronger sentiment features from long-form 10-K Risk Factors than their standard counterparts and prior lexicon-expansion approaches, improving downstream volatility-prediction performance.
evidence: Definition t̂cdi(t) = tcdi(t) + sum_{t' in R(t)} sim(t,t') tcdi(t') (Section 4.1 eq.3).
Table 1: B̂M25 (Text r2=0.439) outperforms BM25 (r2=0.433) and other standard schemes; extended schemes 'hat' improve normal forms.
Table 2: Our Text-only method (r2=0.439) beats Wang (0.345) and Tsai (0.395).
uncertainty_flags: No statistical significance tests or confidence intervals reported for r2 differences vs prior methods.
Performance might depend on embedding training choices (corpus, dims), threshold=0.70 and top-20 neighbor choice—sensitivity analysis not shown.

identified_claims.claim_label: text+market fusion via stacking yields further gains
identified_claims.claim_text: Combining textual features from 10-K Risk Factors with market-derived features using stacking yields additional predictive performance and more stable long-horizon predictions than market-only or text-only models.
evidence: Stacking procedure described (70%-30% split for base/meta training) in Section 4.3.
Table 2: Text+Market Our method r2=0.527 vs Text r2=0.439 and Market r2=0.485.
Figure 2a: Text+Market curve higher and decays slower across quartiles than Market/GARCH baselines.
uncertainty_flags: No CI or fold-level variance for stacked vs other fusion strategies; stacking split may reduce base-model training data and its impact is not quantified.
Potential hyperparameter tuning differences between modalities/baselines not exhaustively reported.

identified_claims.claim_text: Reports from recent years (2012–2015) form a coherent cluster and training on this cluster yields better predictive performance than including older years due to conceptual drift; thus restricting training to 2012–2015 (3892 reports) improves results.
evidence: Figure 1a: cosine similarity heatmap shows clusters 2006–2008, 2009–2011, 2012–2015.
Figure 1b: r2 improves when progressively dropping older years; authors select 2012–2015 for remaining experiments.
uncertainty_flags: Clustering based on Tsai & Wang feature representation—choice of representation may bias cluster structure.
No formal concept-drift statistical test or out-of-sample future-year holdout beyond shown temporal-split experiments.

identified_claims.claim_text: The best-performing pipeline uses B̂M25 weighting with LexExt lexicon, PCA reduction to 400 dimensions, SVM-RBF base learners, and stacking for fusion; this configuration achieves the reported top results.
evidence: Method descriptions: B̂M25 defined by replacing tcdi with t̂cdi; LexExt is lexicon expanded with top-20 Word2Vec neighbors (Section 4.1).
Authors state initial experiments show 400 PCA dims optimal and select B̂M25+LexExt+stacking (Section 6.2).
Table 1/2 present these as top-performing combinations.
uncertainty_flags: Details of the PCA sweep, cross-validated selection protocol for 400 dims, and SVM hyperparameter tuning per baseline are underreported.
Effect of using PCA on interpretability and potential leakage (PCA fit across CV folds?) not clarified.

identified_claims.claim_label: sectoral patterns exist but sector-specific models underperform
identified_claims.claim_text: Financial sectors exhibit distinct risk-term patterns and term-sense disambiguations, but sector-specific models trained on current per-sector data do not outperform a general model—likely due to limited per-sector training sizes; sector-aware analysis still reveals interpretable term importances.
evidence: Figure 2c: per-sector r2 differences for Text and Text+Market.
Figures 3a/3b: sector-specific models are lower than general model; sector-agnostic same-size samples often match sector-specific performance.
Term examples: 'fire' high coefficient in energy; 'beneficial' negative in healthcare/basic industries due to 'beneficial owner' usage.
uncertainty_flags: Attribution of underperformance to sample size is plausible but not isolated—other causes (overfitting, domain mismatch) not ruled out.
Linear-regression coefficient interpretability may be confounded by stemming and multicollinearity when no dimensionality reduction is applied.

identified_claims.claim_text: Text-derived features from 10-K Risk Factors provide a more stable predictive signal over longer horizons compared to market-only models; fusing text with market features reduces performance decay at longer horizons.
evidence: Figure 2a: GARCH and Market performance decay faster across 8 quartiles than Text; Text+Market decays less than Market alone.
Authors' narrative: market-based methods decrease faster as historic prices become less relevant; textual features maintain similar performance across the first year.
uncertainty_flags: No confidence bands or formal time-series tests for trend significance; results may be sample-specific or sensitive to quartile/horizon definitions.
Quartiles defined as fixed 64 trading-day windows; alternative windowing could alter temporal stability observations.

strengths.title: Coherent transfer of embedding-augmented IR to sentiment for long documents
strengths.description: The paper innovatively adapts IR weighting extensions that inject embedding-based term similarity into lexicon-based sentiment features, a theoretically coherent step for long, redundant 10-K Risk Factors where plain token counts underrepresent semantic nuance.
evidence: Equation 3 t̂cdi construction (Section 4.1); citation to Rekabsaz et al. for precedent of embedding-aware IR weights.
Observed improvements for 'hat' variants vs standard forms in Table 1.

strengths.title: Comprehensive empirical pipeline and ablation-style comparisons
strengths.description: The manuscript evaluates multiple weighting formulas (TC/TF/TFIDF/BM25 and their 'hat' versions), several fusion strategies (early, stacking, MKL), and both text-only and text+market settings, giving a broad empirical picture rather than a single cherry-picked result.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 comparing weighting schemes and fusion methods; Figures 2a/2b for temporal behavior; sector experiments in 6.3.

strengths.title: Temporal and sectoral examinations provide useful dataset characterization
strengths.description: By inspecting year-centroid similarities and sector performance, the authors surface concept-drift structure and domain-specific term-sense phenomena that are practically important for future work.
evidence: Figure 1a clustering and Figure 1b performance-by-year; sector term examples ('fire', 'beneficial') and sampling experiments (Figures 3a/3b).

concerns.title: Lack of statistical significance and uncertainty quantification
concerns.description: Key performance differences (e.g., our method vs Tsai/Wang; stacking vs MKL/early fusion) are reported as point estimates without confidence intervals, fold-level variance, or hypothesis tests, making it hard to assess robustness and practical significance.
evidence: Tables 1 and 2 present r2/MSE averages but no standard deviations, CIs, or p-values.
Figures (quartile curves) lack confidence bands.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Report per-fold r2 and MSE standard deviations (or 95% CIs) and run paired statistical tests (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank or bootstrap) comparing top methods; add shaded confidence bands to quartile curves.

concerns.title: Sensitivity of gains to embedding/expansion hyperparameters
concerns.description: The central technique (embedding expansion) depends on Word2Vec choices (window, dimensions, corpus), threshold (0.70), and neighbor count (top-20). No sensitivity/sanity checks are provided to show the effect of these choices on t̂cdi and downstream performance.
evidence: Section 4.1 states threshold 0.70 and top-20 from prior Rekabsaz/Tsai but no experiments vary these parameters.
Assumption A1 flags risk if embeddings are noisy or threshold miscalibrated.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Add ablation experiments varying embedding dimension, training window, similarity threshold (e.g., 0.60, 0.70, 0.80), and neighbor counts (5, 10, 20) and report how these affect r2 and feature interpretability.

concerns.title: Temporal-split protocol and potential leakage
concerns.description: Although the paper presents cross-validation and a few forward-year experiments, the CV protocol may permit temporal leakage (reports from same company across years in both train/test folds) and the PCA/SVM pipeline may be fit improperly across folds, risking optimistic estimates.
evidence: Section 5 states 5-fold CV and PCA to 400 dims but does not clarify whether PCA and Word2Vec training are repeated within each CV fold or fit on full data.
Temporal experiments shown for single-year holdouts (2013/2014/2015) but no strict future-only test set across multiple years.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Clarify and re-run experiments with time-aware splits (train only on data preceding test-year), ensure Word2Vec and PCA are trained exclusively on training folds, and provide company-level partitioning checks to avoid same-company leakage.

concerns.title: Insufficient ablation isolating embedding expansion's marginal benefit
concerns.description: The pipeline includes multiple steps (LexExt expansion, embedding-augmented t̂cdi, PCA, SVM-RBF). The marginal contribution of embedding-augmented term-weighting relative to simple LexExt or to different PCA dims is not isolated clearly.
evidence: Tables compare 'hat' vs standard weights but selected best configuration also includes LexExt, PCA(400), and stacking; interactions not fully decomposed.
Assumptions A3/A1 suggest possible entanglement of gains.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Run controlled ablations: (a) Lex vs LexExt without embedding-augmented t̂cdi, (b) standard BM25 vs B̂M25 without PCA, and (c) PCA dims sweep with/without 'hat' augmentation to report marginal gains.

concerns.title: Risk-factor extraction and volatility-label filtering under-specified
concerns.description: Extraction of Item 1A Risk Factors via term-matching heuristics and the removal of volatility outliers (> mean ± 3σ) are briefly noted but not analyzed; both steps could bias feature quality and label distribution, especially for tail-risk events which are important in volatility contexts.
evidence: Section 5 reports term-matching heuristics for extraction and filtering of volatility extremes but provides no extraction accuracy estimate or alternative thresholds analysis.
Assumption A2/A5 identifies potential contamination or label bias.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: Provide a small manually-annotated extraction validation (precision/recall of Risk Factors extraction), and sensitivity tests for outlier removal (e.g., no filtering, ±4σ) showing how reported r2 changes.

concerns.title: Interpretability concerns from PCA and stemming for sector coefficients
concerns.description: Sectoral term-importance claims rely on linear-regression coefficients learned without PCA to preserve interpretability, but stemming and multi-collinearity can distort coefficients (e.g., 'fire' ambiguity), and earlier PCA steps used in the main pipeline hide features used for predictive gains.
evidence: Section 6.3 shows interpretable coefficients but also uses stemming (Porter) and reports ambiguity examples.
Assumption A3/A9 note PCA and stemming influences.
concerns.actionable_suggestion: When presenting interpretable term coefficients, include feature collinearity diagnostics (VIFs), unstemmed examples, and contrast interpretability models with predictive (PCA-based) models to clarify where interpretability is derived.
